verdict: JPMorgan earned $14.6B as trading revenue surged and banking fees grew — reported revenue rose 8% to $45.3B, and the bank still lifted profit 9% while setting aside $3.3B for possible loan losses.
costNodePlain: Money set aside for loans that may not be repaid — the provision for credit losses: $2.3B of loans were charged off in the quarter and $973M was added to reserves.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: reported basis, vs a year ago

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: Interest earned on loans and securities, minus the interest paid on deposits and borrowings — the bank's core engine, up 1% as balance growth offset lower rates and deposit margin compression.

segments.name: Noninterest revenue
segments.note: Fees, trading and asset-management income — up 17% as Markets revenue rose 21% to $9.7B, asset management fees grew and a $588M First Republic-related gain was included.

opex.name: Compensation expense
opex.note: Pay and benefits for the bank's workforce — its biggest cost.

opex.name: Technology, communications & equipment
opex.note: Technology, telecoms and equipment as the bank invests in AI and its platforms.

opex.name: Occupancy & other expense
opex.note: Branches and offices ($1,302M of occupancy) plus other general costs ($1,481M).

footerNote: JPMorgan headlines 'managed' revenue of $46.0B; this page uses reported (GAAP) revenue of $45.3B — the difference is a tax gross-up that does not change net income. For a bank, credit costs (the provision for credit losses) play the role of cost of revenue, and 'operating profit' here is income before income taxes.
follow100Note: JPMorgan reports revenue two ways: $45.3B reported (GAAP), used here, or $46.0B on a 'managed' basis that grosses up tax-exempt income. Net income is identical either way. The rows reconcile to the $100 total within a cent of rounding.

takeaways.title: Markets had a huge quarter
takeaways.text: Markets revenue rose 21% to $9.7B, led by equities, and investment banking and asset-management fees both grew — the fee engine powered the quarter.

takeaways.title: More set aside for bad loans
takeaways.text: The provision for credit losses rose to $3.3B, from $1.9B a year ago — $2.3B of loans were charged off, mostly in cards, and $973M was added to reserves as the economic outlook darkened a touch.

takeaways.title: Profitability stayed elite
takeaways.text: Return on tangible common equity was 21%, and the bank kept $14.6B — about 32 cents of every reported revenue dollar — while absorbing the bigger credit provision.
